title: Monte Carlo
motto: Dynamic programming needs a model. Monte Carlo needs nothing but episodes. Run the policy, watch the returns, average them. The simplest idea in RL — and the one that unlocks everything downstream.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Dynamic programming needs a model. Monte Carlo needs nothing but episodes. Run the policy, watch the returns, average them. The simplest idea in RL — and the one that unlocks everything downstream.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Dynamic programming is elegant, but it assumes you can query `P(s' | s, a)` for every state and action. Almost nothing in the real world works that way. A robot cannot analytically compute the distribution over camera pixels after a joint torque. A pricing algorithm cannot integrate over every possible customer reaction. An LLM cannot enumerate all possible continuations after a token.

You need a method that only needs the ability to *sample* from the environment. Run the policy. Get a trajectory `s_0, a_0, r_1, s_1, a_1, r_2, …, s_T`. Use it to estimate values. That is Monte Carlo.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Estimate returns from episode samples — no bootstrapping.
